newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portucel '96 loss seen 1.4-1.8 bln esc.
newsitem.headline: Portucel '96 loss seen 1.4-1.8 bln esc.

text.p: Portuguese pulp group Portucel Industrial (PI) is expected to post a loss of between 1.4 and 1.8 billion escudos in 1996 because of drops in pulp prices, but should recover to make a profit in 1997, analysts said.
PI is expected to distribute a dividend of between eight and 20 escudos per share for 1996 when it announces its results on February 25, they said.
PI's results were hit by a sharp increase in pulp stocks, which led to a drastic fall in prices, and by the company's heavy import of timber at high prices, analysts said.
Prices of white eucalyptus pulp fluctuated between 300 and 690 ecus in 1996.
Teresa Pinto Leite of Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) forecast 1996 losses of between 1.5 and 1.6 billion escudos.
"PI's 1996 losses are due to a rise in stocks and a fall in pulp prices," she said.
"Although timber prices fell heavily on the spot market, average costs of timber paid by the company were very high in 1996," she added.

In a recent report Salomon Brothers, which recommended the purchase of PI shares at 955 escudos per share, forecast that PI would post a loss of 1.56 billion escudos in 1996 and distribute a dividend of 15 escudos per share for 1996 and 1997.
Another analyst, who asked not to be identified, forecast that PI would post a loss of between 1.35 and 1.65 billion escudos.
BPI's Pinto Leite said PI could make a profit in 1997.
"In 1997, even if pulp prices do not rise, Portucel could manage to make a profit, because the average cost of imported timber has fallen," she said.
Salomon has forecast that PI will post a profit of 560 million escudos in 1997 and 10 billion in 1998.
Lisbon broker Central de Investimentos has forecast a profit of 5.4 billion escudos in 1997 and another broker Tottadealer has forecast a 1997 profit of 3.9 billion escudos.
Salomon said that improving economic conditions in Europe would help absorb excess pulp capacity and improve capacity utilisation.
PI shares stood at 1,029 escudos, up four, in volume of 102,710 on Lisbon bourse at 1200 GMT.
